fix_commit_message:
[autofit] Prevent signed integer overflow.

Reported as

  https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/471525116

* src/autofit/aflatin.c (af_latin_stretch_top_tilde,
  af_latin_stretch_bottom_tilde): Use `MUL_LONG`.
agent_reasoning: The bug-introducing commit added the tilde-unflattening algorithm, including `af_latin_stretch_tilde`, which computed `( p->y - min_y ) * target_height / height` using raw signed multiplication with a comment incorrectly asserting the values are always small. The fix commit (7b72c0f2) replaces this raw multiplication with `MUL_LONG` (plus `ADD_LONG`/`SUB_LONG`) in the two functions that existed at fix time (`af_latin_stretch_top_tilde` and `af_latin_stretch_bottom_tilde`, which are the post-refactor split of the original `af_latin_stretch_tilde`). Since the on-disk worktree is at the bug-introducing commit, only the single `af_latin_stretch_tilde` function exists (the top/bottom split happened in a later, unrelated commit). I applied the equivalent fix — using `MUL_LONG`/`ADD_LONG`/`SUB_LONG` instead of raw arithmetic, and updated the comment to match the fix's wording — to this single function, since it is the direct ancestor of both functions touched by the fix. This preserves the same conceptual security fix without introducing the unrelated top/bottom refactor, and without modifying any test files.
